In Islam, seeking medical help—including calling an ambulance—is **highly encouraged** when it is necessary for saving a life or alleviating suffering. This aligns with the following principles: 1. **Preservation of Life (Hifz al-Nafs)** – Islam places great importance on protecting life, as it is a divine trust (amanah). The Prophet (ﷺ) said: *"There is no disease that Allah has sent down except that He also sent down its treatment."* (Sahih al-Bukhari) Seeking medical help is a form of fulfilling this duty. 2. **Relief of Suffering** – Islam encourages alleviating pain and distress, especially for one’s own family. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: *"Help your brother, whether he is an oppressor or oppressed."* (Sahih Muslim) Calling an ambulance for your son is an act of compassion and responsibility. 3. **No Harm, No Reciprocation (La Darar wa La Dirar)** – Islam prohibits causing harm, and seeking medical aid is a way to prevent further harm. 4. **Trust in Allah While Taking Rational Action** – While relying on Allah’s will, Muslims are encouraged to take reasonable steps to preserve life, as the Prophet (ﷺ) said: *"The hands of the benevolent are over the hands of the one who is in need."* (Sahih al-Bukhari) ### Answer: **1 (Right)** Calling an ambulance in this scenario is **morally right and obligatory** in Islam, as it aligns with the preservation of life, compassion, and ethical duty.
